_note: Week of Nov. 16 capsules, written from the frozen fact sheet in 2026-11-16.json.
lipscomb:
Lipscomb is 3-2, has won three straight, and is the only team in the ASUN with a positive Bricks Index this week, which says something about the Bisons and something about the league's first two weeks. The case is simple and fresh. On Saturday Lipscomb won at Western Carolina, 75-68, in the mountains of North Carolina, and because the win is only days old it carries nearly full weight: 1.5 points a game on the road ledger. Recent form is plus-1.0. The total, plus-2.5, is first by three points.

The week began at home on Tuesday with an 88-75 win over Belmont, the crosstown rival, in the game Nashville calls the Battle of the Boulevard. Thirteen points in a rivalry game is a comfortable margin in a game that is rarely comfortable.

The scoring has an unusual shape. Takai Simpkins, a senior guard, leads at 17.0 points a game. Right behind him is a freshman forward, Devyn Martin, at 16.0 points and 8.2 rebounds in four games, the kind of debut line that makes a coaching staff quietly rewrite its plans for the next three years. Titas Sargiunas, a senior forward, adds 11.4 points and 2.4 assists.

A senior guard and a freshman forward carrying the scoring together is the sort of pairing that tends to grow more dangerous as the year goes on, because one of them keeps getting better and the other knows how to win.

The week is the busiest on the ASUN card. Tuesday the Bisons go to Purdue, a road game against one of the Big Ten's flagship programs. Friday they play at Alabama A&M. Sunday Milligan, a non-Division I opponent, visits.

Purdue is the long shot, and the formula prices it accordingly. Alabama A&M is the one to win. Lipscomb has found the road agrees with it. This week the road gets longer.
fgcu:
FGCU is 2-3 and second in the ASUN, and if that sounds like a contradiction, it is mostly a measure of how hard the league's early schedule has been on everyone. The Eagles have no road wins yet, so their Bricks Index is all recent form: minus-0.5 points a game, a hair under average, and better than every team in the conference except Lipscomb.

The week had its bumps. On Monday FGCU went to Georgia and lost 80-72, an eight-point road loss to an SEC team that the model treats as a respectable night's work. On Friday the Eagles came home and lost to Florida International, 89-80. On Sunday they beat Abraham Baldwin Agricultural, a non-Division I opponent, 99-31.

The Georgia game is the one that explains the ranking. Losing by eight on an SEC floor is the kind of result a short-memory model reads as a sign of a decent team, and it is why the Eagles sit above teams with better records.

The frontcourt is where the scoring comes from. Chase Konieczny, a sophomore forward, leads at 17.2 points and 5.0 rebounds. Bryson Lucas, a senior forward, adds 14.8 points and 6.8 rebounds. Justin Houser, a sophomore center, is at 12.8 points and 5.2 rebounds. Three big men in double figures is an unusual thing in a sport that has spent the last decade moving away from the basket, and it gives the Eagles a shape that other teams in the league will have to account for.

The week brings one game, and it is an in-state road trip. On Wednesday FGCU plays at Florida Atlantic, a chance to put the first road win on the ledger.

A win in Boca Raton would move the Eagles closer to Lipscomb. A loss would keep them where they are. Either way, Konieczny will get his touches. The question is whether the rest of the floor opens up around him.
west-florida:
West Florida lost two games last week by a combined four points, and if there is a crueler way to spend a week in college basketball, it has not been invented yet. On Thursday the Argonauts went to Alabama A&M and lost 85-83. On Friday they met Cleveland State on a neutral floor and lost 69-67. Two two-point losses on consecutive nights.

Before that, on Monday, they had beaten Baptist (Fl), a non-Division I opponent, 110-59. It was a fine evening that the model mostly ignores.

The Bricks Index has the Argonauts at minus-2.4 points a game, all recent form, no road credit, third in the ASUN. That is a number built on games that could have gone either way, and a couple of made free throws would have made it a very different one.

The scoring runs through one player. DJ Shine, a junior guard, is averaging 17.4 points a game over five games, nearly double anyone else on the roster. Jay King, a senior guard, is at 9.5 points. Alex Godley Jr., a senior guard, adds 9.4. Shine is the kind of scorer who can carry a team through a close game, and the Argonauts have played enough close games already to know they will need him to.

The question with a team like this is whether the close losses become close wins over time. Two-point games have a way of evening out across a season, and a team that keeps putting itself in them is a team that will win its share.

The week brings Green Bay to Pensacola on Tuesday, a home game against a Horizon team. On Sunday the Argonauts go to South Alabama, a short trip along the Gulf Coast and a chance at a first road win.

Two games, two chances. After last week, the Argonauts would settle for a game that is not decided in the final possession. They will probably not get one.
jacksonville:
Jacksonville is 2-1, fourth in the ASUN, and has played only one game in the past week, a 79-61 home win over Kansas City on Monday. It was an eighteen-point win over a Division I opponent, the kind of result that a short-memory model takes seriously. The Dolphins have no road wins yet, so the index is all recent form: minus-2.5 points a game.

That is a team that has not been tested much yet, and the Bricks Index is waiting, along with everyone else, to see what happens when it is.

The scoring is spread across three players. Hayden Wood, a sophomore guard, leads at 16.0 points and 5.0 rebounds. Jamie Phillips Jr., a junior guard, adds 15.3 points and 2.7 assists. Nehemiah Turner, a junior forward, is at 11.0. Two guards scoring fifteen or more a night is a backcourt that can carry a team through long stretches, and both of them are young enough to keep getting better.

The Kansas City game was the template: a home floor, a Division I opponent, and a margin wide enough that the last five minutes were a formality. What the Dolphins have not had yet is a game that asked them to win on the road or come back from behind.

The week is the busiest the Dolphins have had. On Monday, the day this ranking was frozen, they play at Georgia, an SEC team on its own floor, the kind of road opponent the Index pays very well for. On Thursday Little Rock visits. On Saturday Central Arkansas comes in.

Three games in six days is a real test for a team that has played only three games all season. By Sunday the Dolphins will have doubled their sample size, and the Index will have a much clearer idea of who they are. So will they.
queens:
Queens is a team that likes to score, and the ledger shows it. The Royals beat Winthrop 103-98 on a neutral floor on Nov. 2, then won at Loyola Marymount 96-95 on Nov. 4, and on Saturday they came home and beat Wofford 97-92. In between, on Tuesday, they went to BYU and lost 98-82. In three of those four games, Queens scored 96 or more.

The two early road wins are worth 1.1 points a game on the ledger, the second-most road credit in the ASUN. Recent form, though, is minus-3.8, weighed down by the points the Royals allow, which in their last four games have never been fewer than 92. The total is minus-2.7, fifth in the league.

That is a fair description of a team that plays at a sprint and lets the scoreboard sort it out. In November, that is fun to watch. In February, it tends to depend on who is shooting well that night.

The guards do the scoring. Nasir Mann, a senior, leads at 18.2 points a game. Jordan Watford, a sophomore, adds 14.6 points and 5.6 assists, the playmaker who keeps the pace high. Caleb Jones, a freshman, is at 14.0 points, a first-year player already trusted to take shots in a system that requires a lot of them.

Three guards averaging fourteen or more is the engine of a team built to outrun people. What it needs is enough stops to make the running count.

The week brings one game, and it is a big one. On Saturday Queens plays at LSU, an SEC team on its own floor, the kind of road opponent the formula prices generously. The Royals will not change their style for the occasion. They never do.

A win in Baton Rouge would be one of the biggest road results in the ASUN this season. A loss would cost little. Either way, it will probably be high scoring.
bellarmine:
Bellarmine is 1-4, sixth in the ASUN, and the record is a fair reflection of a difficult start. On Wednesday the Knights beat Franklin, a non-Division I opponent, 99-82 at home. On Saturday they hosted Northern Illinois and lost 72-64. The Bricks Index has them at minus-9.9 points a game, all recent form, no road credit.

There is no sense in pretending the number is better than it is. There is also no sense in reading it as a final judgment, because five games is a small sample.

The scoring is spread thin. Tyler Doyle, a junior guard, leads at 12.6 points, 4.2 rebounds and 3.2 assists, the all-around line of a player who does a little of everything. Sam Donald, a sophomore forward, adds 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. Kenyon Goodin, a junior guard, is at 9.4. No one is carrying the team alone, which means the Knights have not yet found the player who takes over when the game gets close.

That player may emerge. In a season of thirty games, the first five are mostly about finding out who you are, and Bellarmine is still finding out.

The week is two road games. On Tuesday the Knights play at Illinois State, a Missouri Valley program on its own floor. On Friday they go to Eastern Kentucky, a short drive across the Bluegrass.

Both are the kind of road games that the Index rewards, and a win in either would put the Knights on the ledger for the first time this season. Doyle will need help to get there. The Northern Illinois game showed the Knights can stay close with a team that has won at Dayton this year. The next step is finishing.
north-florida:
North Florida is 1-3, has lost three straight, and is seventh in the ASUN, which tells you where the Ospreys are without telling you much about where they are headed. The one win came on Nov. 3 at California Baptist, 71-63, a road win that is still on the ledger at 0.3 points a game. Recent form is minus-10.9. The total is minus-10.7.

Last week was hard. On Monday the Ospreys went to Miami and lost 89-51, an ACC opponent on its home floor, the sort of night a team gets through and moves on from. On Saturday they came home and lost to The Citadel, 77-74, a three-point loss that hurt more for being close.

The scoring is spread among the guards. Kent Jackson, a junior, leads at 11.2 points and 2.5 assists. JR Bartelus, another junior, adds 10.2 points and 3.8 rebounds. Mason Lee, a senior, is at 8.3 points and 4.3 rebounds in three games. It is a roster still looking for a go-to scorer, and in the meantime it wins and loses as a group.

There is a familiar pattern for teams like this one. The losses come early, while the rotation is still being sorted out, and then, sometime around the turn of the year, the right five players find each other and the games start to tip the other way. The Citadel game, lost by three, is the kind that turns around once a team figures out its late-game roles.

The week offers two home games. On Tuesday Fort Lauderdale visits. On Saturday Little Rock comes in. Neither will move the road ledger, but both are chances to end the streak in front of the home crowd.

The Cal Baptist win showed this team can win on the road. Now it needs to show it can win at home. Saturday would be a good day to start.
stetson:
Stetson is 0-4, eighth in the ASUN, and still waiting for its first win. The Hatters went to Howard on Thursday and lost 75-62, the only game they played last week. The Bricks Index has them at minus-11.1 points a game, all recent form, no road credit.

Every season has a team that starts slowly, and the early weeks of November are not kind to anyone whose rotation is still coming together. Four games is a small sample. It is also four losses, and there is no point pretending otherwise.

What the box score shows is a team built around two senior forwards. Collin Kuhl leads at 16.0 points and 5.8 rebounds, the steady inside presence that a team can build around. Magnus Entenmann adds 10.2 points and 6.0 rebounds. Thiago Sucatzky, a sophomore guard, is at 6.5 points and 4.8 assists, the player who gets the ball to the forwards where they want it.

Two experienced forwards and a young guard who knows how to feed them is a reasonable structure for a team. What it has not had yet is the night when the shots fall and the defense holds at the same time.

The week brings two games. On Monday, the day this ranking was frozen, Florida Memorial, a non-Division I opponent, visits DeLand. That is the most likely place for the first win to arrive. On Thursday the Hatters go to Louisville, an ACC program in a big building, the sort of road game the formula prices as generously as any.

The Louisville game is the long shot. The Florida Memorial game is the one that matters most, because the first win is always the hardest one, and the rest tend to follow more easily once it arrives.

Kuhl is a senior. He knows that. The Hatters would like to make this the week the waiting ends.
